name: Mudu Koraga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record mudu1241 and family record kora1289
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's most extensive description for mudu1241 = Bhat 1971 (grammar sketch, 14 pp.); Koraga subgroup = Korra Koraga [korr1238][kfd] (dialects Ande, Onti, Tappu) + Mudu Koraga [mudu1241][vmd]; coordinates 12.62 N 75.11 E (Kasaragod side).

sources.citation: KIRTADS Linguistic Cell (prep. Shyam S. K; ed. Pugazhendi et al.). 2019. Pasaru (Butterfly): Koraga Bhasha Sahayi -- Preparation of Handbook for Koraga language of Koraga Community in Kerala State. Kozhikode: KIRTADS. ISBN 978-81-936765-9-2. 296 pp., Malayalam.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 11 'Bhasha' (p. 44 ff.) cites Bhat 1971's four dialects, then lists 5 short + 5 long vowels, diphthongs and consonants by place/manner with Koraga-Malayalam-English word lists; no section on stress; a full-text search for stress/accent Malayalam stress/accent terms (ഊന്നൽ, സ്വരാഘാതം, ആഘാതം) and English 'stress/accent' returns nothing. Describes the Kasaragod (Kerala) Koraga without saying which Bhat dialect it is.

sources.citation: Bhat, D. N. Shankara. 1971. The Koraga Language. Poona: Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute. 123 pp. (ch. 4 'Mudu Koraga', pp. 33-40; phonology pp. 33-34)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Mudu phonology (sec. 1, pp. 33-34) gives only the phonemic inventory, allophony of n and a, distribution/cluster restrictions and minimal-pair contrasts (length, quality, nasalization, gemination, voicing); the Onti (pp. 4-5) and Tappu (pp. 21-22) phonology sections are the same shape. a full-text search for stress/accent both scanned layers for stress/accent/tone/pitch/intonation/prominence: only 'over-emphasized' (p. 3) and 'equal prominence' (p. 23, about canonical shapes of Tappu verbal bases). No stress marks in texts or vocabulary.

sources.citation: Ethnologue free page for vmd; HathiTrust catalog search 'Koraga language'; OLAC vmd; Phonotacticon 'Korra Koraga'; Kannada Wikipedia 'ಕೊರಗ ಭಾಷೆ'; English Wikipedia 'Koraga language'; KIRTADS Koraga page; archive.org search
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Wikipedia (en, kn) cites only Bhat 1971, Krishnamurti 2003 and Shetty 1978; HathiTrust has a record of Bhat 1971 only; Ethnologue free page has no references; no phonology article, JIPA illustration, thesis or other description of any Koraga variety turned up in twelve DuckDuckGo queries (English and Kannada).

sources.citation: Shetty, Ramakrishna T. 2008. Koraga Grammar (Tribal Language Grammar 1; Dravidian Linguistics Series 1). Kuppam: Dravidian University. xiv, 286 pp. ISBN 9788190639163. (published edition of the 1978 Poona PhD thesis 'Koraga Grammar: a descriptive study of a Dravidian dialect', viii, 375 pp.)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only full-length grammar of any Koraga variety (Glottolog full grammar, 402 pp. thesis); a 1970s Deccan College descriptive grammar of this size normally has a suprasegmentals paragraph. Describes Ande Koraga (Mangalore/Udupi) = Korra Koraga [kfd, korr1238], not mudu1241, so any statement would need an identity note.

sources.citation: Krishnamurti, Bhadriraju. 2003. The Dravidian Languages. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. (ch. 4 Phonology, general remarks on stress in Dravidian)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number PL4601.K76 2003x) (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Standard family handbook (comparative); its general statement that stress is non-distinctive and word-initial in Dravidian could be cited as a family-level default, but it is not Koraga-specific and would be second-hand at best.
